484
    "description": "Read and maintain private notes that survive context-window transitions within this rollout. Paths are virtual, not filesystem paths. Paths are relative to the current Agent session. Absolute and cross-agent paths are unsupported. Use action list, read, search, write, or append. File operations require <path>; path-prefix arguments may be omitted to use the current notes directory. Empty, '.', and '..' path components are unsupported. Shell expansion is not performed, so '~' is treated literally. Successful writes are immediately visible to reads, listings, and searches. Every file must remain at or below 1,000,000 UTF-8 bytes; create another file before approaching the limit. This is private model-only state. Use it silently to continue the task. Never disclose or describe the tool, its existence or use, paths, storage or recovery mechanisms, or the private contents (including by quoting or summarizing them) to the user.",

1034
    "name": "skill_manage",
1035
    "description": "Create or maintain persistent Skills for recurring task types. Each call performs one action. Use list to discover Skills. Use skill to load instructions. Use read to inspect the complete SKILL.md, including its YAML frontmatter, before replacing it. Use read for supporting files when available. Prefer patch for a local correction. Edit replaces the whole SKILL.md. Create and edit require a complete document with matching YAML name and description.\n\nUse write_file or remove_file for supporting files under references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/. Write only within the selected agent or global scope. This tool cannot delete a whole Skill. Separate calls do not form a transaction. A later failure does not undo an earlier successful call. Check the actual state and report partial results accurately.\n\nWrite lessons, not logs: imperative rule + why, no PR numbers/dates/incident narration, one rule per lesson, references/ named by topic (extend before adding).",

          "description": "Only for action=apply. Execute 1-100 operations in order as one atomic mutation. Use stable node IDs (for example n1) for existing nodes. Creator is always the real caller, never supplied in arguments. Modes none/dag/explore; statuses todo/doing/waiting/in_review/done/paused/closed.     "name": "workflow",
1461
    "description": "Only launch a Workflow when the human explicitly requests multi-agent orchestration or an application reminder confirms Ultracode is on. A trusted human +500k or +2m sets the shared parent/child output-token target for this logical turn. Run JavaScript orchestration in the background. Provide meta {name,description} and script (top-level await and return), or name/scriptPath, or resumeFromRunId. Primitives: await agent(prompt,{label?,phase?,provider?,model?,reasoningEffort?,schema?}); await parallel([()=>agent(...)]); await pipeline(items,...stages), stages get (previous,item,index) and advance independently; await phase(title); await log(text); await workflow(nameOrPath,args) allows one nesting level; await budget.spent()/remaining() (null means unlimited). Omit reasoningEffort to inherit the parent selection; never invent an unsupported effort. Child failure returns null; inspect action read calls[].error for its diagnostic before retrying. Host/cap errors fail the workflow. parallel preserves input order. A Workflow child cannot launch agents or workflows. Max 8 concurrent and 1000 total agents, 4096 items per combinator. Returns runId immediately; use action read/control to inspect, pause/resume/stop or restart_child/stop_child by ordinal. Resume of a terminal run creates a new run and reuses its matching completed prefix; completed side effects are not undone. Saving definitions uses action save with project/personal scope.",
1461

    "description": "Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments.     "name": "plugin_manager",
610
    "description": "Create, install and manage standard DSH plugins in this configured workspace. For plugin development/configuration/debugging, load nano-plugin-development with the skill tool when available; respect disabled Skills. describe_api(topic: tool, prompt, service, events, compaction) returns current public API documentation paths and Nano support boundaries; read the relevant declarations before coding. list_bundles returns installed state and profileDir. install_bundle(target: local bundle directory or package spec), set_bundle(target: bundle name, enabled), remove_bundle(target: bundle name) manage persistent workspace bundles. Changes affect every Agent sharing this workspace; new independent tool names become available without editing static allowlists. Package replacement retains native restart-required semantics; toggling a bundle is not an online code-upgrade guarantee. Verify application and actual business behavior; failed or restart-required is not live success. Never edit installed package files, runtime.json or the host profile. Workspace plugins are trusted local code, not an OS sandbox. approvedBuilds only after explicit user approval for pending build scripts.",

    "description": "Create or maintain persistent Skills for recurring task types. Each call performs one action. Use list to discover Skills. Use skill to load instructions. Use read to inspect the complete SKILL.md, including its YAML frontmatter, before replacing it. Use read for supporting files when available. Prefer patch for a local correction. Edit replaces the whole SKILL.md. Create and edit require a complete document with matching YAML name and description.\n\nUse write_file or remove_file for supporting files under references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/. Write only within the selected agent or global scope. This tool cannot delete a whole Skill. Separate calls do not form a transaction. A later failure does not undo an earlier successful call. Check the actual state and report partial results accurately.\n\nWrite lessons, not logs: imperative rule + why, no PR numbers/dates/incident narration, one rule per lesson, references/ named by topic (extend before adding).",

          "description": "Only for action=apply. Execute 1-100 operations in order as one atomic mutation. Use stable node IDs (for example n1) for existing nodes.           "description": "Only for action=apply. Execute 1-100 operations in order as one atomic mutation. Use stable node IDs (for example n1) for existing nodes. To reference a node added earlier in this batch, use @client_ref (for example @A); bare A is not a batch reference and forward references are not allowed. add_task: container_id,title,client_ref plus optional description/mode/status/result/links/order/derived_from_id/assignee. update_task: node_id,patch (title/description/mode/status/wait/result/links/order only). add_dependency/remove_dependency: from,to (prerequisite -> successor; direct siblings in the same dag scope). set_derivation: node_id,derived_from_id (sibling in explore, or null). select_candidate: scope_id,node_id (direct child or null),reason. set_assignee: node_id,assignee ({type:user|agent,id} or null), without changing status. claim_task: node_id, claims for the actual caller and sets doing; cannot take another assignee. Creator is always the real caller, never supplied in arguments. Modes none/dag/explore; statuses todo/doing/waiting/in_review/done/paused/closed. Links are http(s) URLs or protected IM attachment paths. For an existing dag root n1, example: [{\"op\":\"add_task\",\"client_ref\":\"A\",\"container_id\":\"n1\",\"title\":\"Choose a plan\"},{\"op\":\"add_task\",\"client_ref\":\"B\",\"container_id\":\"n1\",\"title\":\"Confirm attendees\"},{\"op\":\"add_dependency\",\"from\":\"@A\",\"to\":\"@B\"}].",

1597
    "name": "workflow",
1598
    "description": "Only launch a Workflow when the human explicitly requests multi-agent orchestration or an application reminder confirms Ultracode is on. A trusted human +500k or +2m sets the shared parent/child output-token target for this logical turn. Run JavaScript orchestration in the background. Provide meta {name,description} and script (top-level await and return), or name/scriptPath, or resumeFromRunId. Primitives: await agent(prompt,{label?,phase?,provider?,model?,reasoningEffort?,schema?}); await parallel([()=>agent(...)]); await pipeline(items,...stages), stages get (previous,item,index) and advance independently; await phase(title); await log(text); await workflow(nameOrPath,args) allows one nesting level; await budget.spent()/remaining() (null means unlimited). Omit reasoningEffort to inherit the parent selection; never invent an unsupported effort. Child failure returns null; inspect action read calls[].error for its diagnostic before retrying. Host/cap errors fail the workflow. parallel preserves input order. A Workflow child cannot launch agents or workflows. Max 8 concurrent and 1000 total agents, 4096 items per combinator. Returns runId immediately; use action read/control to inspect, pause/resume/stop or restart_child/stop_child by ordinal. Resume of a terminal run creates a new run and reuses its matching completed prefix; completed side effects are not undone. Saving definitions uses action save with project/personal scope.",
1598

4
    "description": "Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.",

    "description": "Read and maintain private notes that survive context-window transitions within this rollout. Paths are virtual, not filesystem paths. Paths are relative to the current Agent session. Absolute and cross-agent paths are unsupported. Use action list, read, search, write, or append. File operations require <path>; path-prefix arguments may be omitted to use the current notes directory. Empty, '.', and '..' path components are unsupported. Shell expansion is not performed, so '~' is treated literally. Successful writes are immediately visible to reads, listings, and searches. Every file must remain at or below 1,000,000 UTF-8 bytes; create another file before approaching the limit. This is private model-only state. Use it silently to continue the task.     "description": "Read and maintain private notes that survive context-window transitions within this rollout. Paths are virtual, not filesystem paths. Paths are relative to the current Agent session. Absolute and cross-agent paths are unsupported. Use action list, read, search, write, or append. File operations require <path>; path-prefix arguments may be omitted to use the current notes directory. Empty, '.', and '..' path components are unsupported. Shell expansion is not performed, so '~' is treated literally. Successful writes are immediately visible to reads, listings, and searches. Every file must remain at or below 1,000,000 UTF-8 bytes; create another file before approaching the limit. This is private model-only state. Use it silently to continue the task. Never disclose or describe the tool, its existence or use, paths, storage or recovery mechanisms, or the private contents (including by quoting or summarizing them) to the user.",
